Line a loaf tin with plastic wrap. Mash two thirds of the raspberries.
Whisk the eggs and sugar in a bowl over simmering water until thick, pale and hot to the touch (about 70°C/160°F), then whisk until cool.
Whip the cream with the vanilla and fold into the eggs, then fold in the mashed raspberries and whole berries.
Freeze at least 6 hours and slice to serve.
Brush the cut sides of the peaches with oil.
Grill or griddle cut side down 4 to 6 minutes until charred and softened.
Serve with yogurt, drizzled with honey and pistachios.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Put the plums cut side up in a dish, sprinkle with sugar, add the vanilla, juice and dots of butter.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes until soft and syrupy.
Serve warm with cream or ice cream.
Toss the strawberries with the sugar, balsamic and pepper.
Leave 15 minutes to release their juices.
Scatter with torn basil and serve with mascarpone or ice cream.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F).
Set the pears cut side up in a dish, fill the hollows with walnuts and drizzle with the maple syrup and butter.
Sprinkle with cinnamon and bake 25 to 30 minutes until tender.
Melt the butter with the sugar and cinnamon until bubbling.
Add the bananas and cook 2 minutes a side.
If using rum, take the pan off the heat, add it and carefully return to the heat to bubble off the alcohol (keep a lid handy).
Spoon over ice cream.
Cook half the berries with the sugar for 5 minutes, then cool.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in the yogurt.
Ripple through the cooked and fresh berries and spoon into glasses.
Toss the strawberries with the sugar and leave 10 minutes.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Fold together the cream, meringue and most of the strawberries and pile into glasses with the rest on top.
Toss the pineapple with the sugar.
Cook in the butter in a hot pan 3 to 4 minutes a side until caramelized.
Squeeze over lime and scatter with mint.
Bring the cream to a simmer and pour over the chocolate and butter; stir until smooth.
Chill 2 hours until firm.
Scoop into small balls, roll quickly between your palms and toss in cocoa.
Keep in the fridge.
Bring the butter, sugar, milk and cocoa to a rolling boil and boil exactly 1 minute.
Off the heat stir in the peanut butter, vanilla and oats.
Drop spoonfuls onto parchment and leave 30 minutes to set.
Melt the chocolate, butter and syrup together gently.
Stir in the biscuits, marshmallows and cherries.
Press into a lined 20 cm square tin and chill 2 hours.
Cut into squares.
Whip the cream with the sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
In a loaf tin lined with plastic wrap, layer cookies and cream, finishing with cream.
Chill overnight so the cookies soften into cake.
Turn out and top with grated chocolate.
Mix the crumbs, butter, peanut butter and sugar and press into a lined 20 cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate chips and spread over.
Chill 1 hour and cut into bars.
Stir everything together in a large mug until smooth.
Microwave 60 to 90 seconds until risen and just set; ovens vary, so check after 60 seconds.
Cool 1 minute before eating.
Whisk everything in a large mug.
Microwave 60 to 80 seconds until risen.
Drizzle with a little extra lemon juice mixed with sugar.
Pat the strawberries completely dry.
Melt the dark chocolate in short bursts in the microwave, stirring.
Dip each berry and set on parchment; drizzle with melted white chocolate if you like.
Chill 20 minutes to set.
Put 2 scoops of ice cream in each glass.
Pour a shot of hot espresso over each.
Top with grated chocolate and serve straight away.
Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Mix the crumbs and butter and press into the tin; bake 8 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth, then the eggs, sour cream, vanilla and zest.
Pour over the base and bake 30 to 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble. Cool, then chill 4 hours before cutting.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 20 cm round tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together, then whisk in the sugar.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the cocoa and salt.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until the top is set but the middle is still a little soft. Cool in the tin; it sinks and becomes fudgy.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Roll the pastry to a 30 cm circle on a lined tray.
Toss the apples with the sugar, cinnamon and flour and pile in the middle, leaving a 5 cm border.
Fold the border over the fruit, dot with butter and brush the pastry with egg.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until golden. Brush the apples with warm jam.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Pour the melted butter into a 23 cm round tin, sprinkle with the brown sugar and arrange the pineapple (and cherries) on top.
Cream the soft butter and sugar, beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour and baking powder with the milk.
Spread over the fruit and bake 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes, then turn out onto a plate.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a 23 cm dish.
Spread the cherries in the dish.
Whisk the eggs and sugar, then the flour, then the milk and vanilla to a smooth batter.
Pour over the cherries and bake 35 minutes until puffed and set. Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa.
Melt the chocolate and butter together.
Whisk the 2 eggs, 2 yolks and sugar until thick, fold in the chocolate, then the flour.
Divide between the ramekins and bake 10 to 12 minutes until the edges are firm but the centres wobble. Rest 1 minute and turn out.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a 20 x 30 cm dish.
Soak the dates in the boiling water with the baking soda for 10 minutes.
Cream 50 g butter with 100 g sugar, beat in the eggs, fold in the flour, then the dates and their liquid. Bake 30 to 35 minutes.
For the sauce, simmer the rest of the butter and sugar with the cream and syrup for 3 minutes. Pour over the warm pudding.
Cook the apples with the butter, sugar and cinnamon for 5 minutes until just soft, then cool.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut the pastry into 8 squares.
Put a spoonful of apple on each, fold into triangles and press the edges with a fork.
Brush with egg, cut a small slit in each and bake 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
Heat the oven to 120°C (250°F) and line a tray.
Whisk the whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoonful at a time, whisking to a thick glossy meringue. Fold in the cornstarch and vinegar.
Spread into a 20 cm round with a dip in the middle and bake 75 minutes, then cool in the switched-off oven.
Top with whipped cream and berries just before serving.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and butter a baking dish.
Whisk the milk, cream, eggs, sugar, cocoa and vanilla.
Toss the bread and chocolate chips in the dish, pour over the custard and press down; soak 15 minutes.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until set and crisp on top.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and roll the pastry onto a lined tray.
Sprinkle the almond flour in the middle, leaving a 5 cm border.
Toss the peaches with sugar and cornstarch and pile on top, then fold up the edges.
Brush with egg, scatter with almonds and bake 35 to 40 minutes until golden.
Whip the chickpea liquid with the cream of tartar to soft peaks, about 5 minutes.
Add the sugar gradually and whip to stiff glossy peaks.
Fold in the cooled chocolate gently in three parts.
Spoon into glasses and chill at least 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 240°C (475°F). Roll the pastry into a log, cut into 12 rounds and press each into a muffin tin cup.
Cook the yolks, sugar, cornstarch and milk over medium heat, whisking, until thick, then add the vanilla.
Fill the pastry cups three quarters full.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes until the pastry is crisp and the tops have dark spots. Dust with cinnamon.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and spices in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and lemons, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Scrape into the tin.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and spices in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and bananas, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips and scrape into the tin.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and spices in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and orange, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the cranberries and scrape into the tin.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and spices in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and grated apple, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the diced apple and scrape into the tin.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and spices in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and dates, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the walnuts and scrape into the tin.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and vanilla extract, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Pour half the batter into the tin, stir the cocoa paste into the rest, spoon it on top and swirl with a knife.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and greek yogurt; 1 tsp, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the strawberries and scrape into the tin.
Bake 55 to 65 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 900 g (2 lb) loaf tin.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and spices in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the sugar, eggs, milk, oil and rose water, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Fold in the pistachios and scrape into the tin.
Bake 50 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the tin, then on a rack.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then rub in the butter until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the milk beaten with the egg (keep 1 tbsp for brushing) to make a soft dough; do not overwork it.
Pat out 3 cm thick, cut into 8 wedges or rounds, brush with the reserved egg and bake 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve warm with jam and clotted or whipped cream.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then rub in the butter until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the flavourings and the blueberries, then the milk beaten with the egg (keep 1 tbsp for brushing) to make a soft dough; do not overwork it.
Pat out 3 cm thick, cut into 8 wedges or rounds, brush with the reserved egg and bake 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve warm with butter or lemon curd.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt, then rub in the butter until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the cheddar and chives, then the milk beaten with the egg (keep 1 tbsp for brushing) to make a soft dough; do not overwork it.
Pat out 3 cm thick, cut into 8 wedges or rounds, brush with the reserved egg and bake 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve warm with butter.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then rub in the butter until it looks like breadcrumbs.
Stir in the flavourings and the dried cranberries, then the milk beaten with the egg (keep 1 tbsp for brushing) to make a soft dough; do not overwork it.
Pat out 3 cm thick, cut into 8 wedges or rounds, brush with the reserved egg and bake 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve warm with butter.

Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a tray.
Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then rub in the butter until it looks like breadcrumbs.

Pat out 3 cm thick, cut into 8 wedges or rounds, brush with the reserved egg and bake 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden.
Serve warm with butter and honey.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Melt the butter, sugar and syrup together, then stir in the oats and salt.
Press firmly into the tin and bake 20 to 25 minutes until golden at the edges.
Cut into squares while warm, then cool completely in the tin.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Whisk the butter and sugar, then the egg and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt and chocolate.
Spread in the tin and bake 22 to 25 minutes until golden but still soft in the middle. Cool before cutting.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 20 x 30 cm tin.
Mix the flour, oats, sugar, butter, baking soda and salt into a crumbly dough.
Press two thirds into the tin, spread with jam and scatter the rest over.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden. Cool before slicing.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Rub the flour, sugar and 120 g butter into a dough, press into a lined 20 cm tin and bake 20 to 25 minutes until pale golden.
Melt the rest of the butter with the condensed milk and syrup and cook, stirring constantly, for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and caramel coloured. Pour over the base and chill 1 hour.
Melt the chocolate, spread over and chill until set.
Cut with a hot knife.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Mix the flour, coconut, sugar and butter and press into the tin; bake 12 minutes.
Whisk the condensed milk with the lemon zest and juice and pour over.
Bake 12 minutes more until just set. Chill and cut.
Heat the oven to 170°C (340°F) and line a 20 cm square tin.
Warm the honey, peanut butter and butter until smooth.
Mix with the dry ingredients, press very firmly into the tin and bake 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool completely before cutting into bars.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line two trays.
Cream the butter and sugars, beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt, then the chips.
Roll into balls, space well apart and bake 10 to 11 minutes; they firm up as they cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cream the butter and brown sugar, then beat in the egg and molasses.
Mix in the flour, baking soda and spices.
Roll into balls, roll in sugar and bake 9 to 10 minutes until crackled.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg, zest and juice.
Mix in the flour, baking powder and salt; chill 20 minutes.
Roll into balls, coat thickly in powdered sugar and bake 10 to 11 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Mix everything into a soft dough.
Roll into balls, press with a fork and bake 9 to 10 minutes. Cool on the tray; they are fragile while warm.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, baking soda and salt, then the chocolate and cranberries.
Bake spoonfuls 10 to 11 minutes until golden at the edges.
Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F).
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the yolk and vanilla, then the flour and salt.
Roll into small balls, press a dent in each with your thumb and fill with jam.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes until pale golden.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, oats and chips.
Bake spoonfuls 11 to 12 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and flour a tray.
Mix the flour, baking soda and salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft, sticky dough.
Shape into a round, cut a deep cross on top and bake 35 to 40 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
Cool on a rack wrapped in a tea towel for a soft crust.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk and 30 g butter and knead 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rise 1 hour.
Shape into 12 balls and pack into a buttered dish; rise 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Mix the remaining butter with the garlic and parsley and brush over.
Bake 22 to 25 minutes until golden.
Mix everything into a soft dough and knead 8 minutes. Cover and rise 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 250°C (480°F) with a baking tray inside.
Divide into 8, roll into 15 cm rounds and rest 10 minutes.
Bake 2 or 3 at a time on the hot tray for 4 to 5 minutes until puffed. Wrap in a towel to keep soft.
Mix the flour, yeast, salt, rosemary, water and 2 tbsp oil and knead 10 minutes. Rise 1 hour until doubled.
Shape into a round loaf on a floured tray and rise 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Brush with the rest of the oil and slash the top.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until deep golden.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Spread the pastry with mustard, scatter with cheese and onion and roll up tightly from the long side.
Slice into 12 rounds, lay on a lined tray and brush with egg.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt, then stir in the zucchini, most of the cheese and the green onions.
Whisk the eggs, milk and oil and fold in until just combined.
Spoon into the tin, top with the rest of the cheese and bake 20 to 22 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line two 20 cm round tins.
Beat the butter, sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder and milk until smooth and pale.
Divide between the tins and bake 22 to 25 minutes until springy.
Cool, then sandwich with jam and whipped cream and dust with powdered sugar.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 23 cm round tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in the oil, zest and juice.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Dust with powdered sugar.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 23 cm springform tin.
Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the eggs, then fold in the flour, baking powder and milk.
Spread in the tin, press the apple slices into the batter in rings and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.
Bake 45 to 50 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a 23 cm tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until thick and pale.
Fold in the almond flour, zest and baking powder.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until golden and set. Cool and dust with powdered sugar.

Whisk in the miso off the heat, and ladle over the noodles with the pork, halved eggs, green onions and nori.

Pour in the water, keeping below the max line and scrape the bottom of the inner pot clean, so nothing is stuck and the pot doesn't show a burn warning. An electric pressure cooker needs at least 1 cup (250 ml) of thin liquid to come up to pressure.
Add the bones, brisket, onion, ginger and spices.
Lock the lid and turn the valve to Sealing. Pressure cook on High for 45 minutes. The pot first takes about 10 to 15 minutes to come up to pressure; that is not part of the cook time.
Let the pressure release naturally for about 15 minutes, until the float valve drops, then open the lid.
Lift out the brisket and slice thinly, strain the broth, and season with fish sauce and sugar.
Pour over the noodles and brisket and serve with herbs, sprouts and lime.
Select Sauté and heat the pot. Heat the oil and brown the pork, then add the sugar and cook until it caramelises, about 2 minutes. Stir in the garlic and ginger.

Pour in the water, soy sauces and wine and scrape the bottom of the inner pot clean, so nothing is stuck and the pot doesn't show a burn warning. An electric pressure cooker needs at least 1 cup (250 ml) of thin liquid to come up to pressure.
Add the star anise.
Lock the lid and turn the valve to Sealing. Pressure cook on High for 25 minutes. The pot first takes about 10 to 15 minutes to come up to pressure; that is not part of the cook time.
Let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes, then quick release the rest and open the lid carefully.
Reduce the sauce on Sauté until sticky and scatter with green onions.

Pour in the stock and scrape the bottom of the inner pot clean, so nothing is stuck and the pot doesn't show a burn warning. An electric pressure cooker needs at least 1 cup (250 ml) of thin liquid to come up to pressure.
Add the rice, chicken and half the ginger.
Lock the lid and turn the valve to Sealing. Pressure cook on High for 30 minutes. The pot first takes about 10 to 15 minutes to come up to pressure; that is not part of the cook time.
Let the pressure release naturally for about 15 minutes, until the float valve drops, then open the lid.
Shred the chicken into the congee, season, and top with ginger, green onions, soy and sesame oil.

Pour in the water and scrape the bottom of the inner pot clean, so nothing is stuck and the pot doesn't show a burn warning. An electric pressure cooker needs at least 1 cup (250 ml) of thin liquid to come up to pressure.
Add the unsoaked chickpeas and baking soda (it makes them extra soft).
Lock the lid and turn the valve to Sealing. Pressure cook on High for 45 minutes. The pot first takes about 10 to 15 minutes to come up to pressure; that is not part of the cook time.
Let the pressure release naturally for about 15 minutes, until the float valve drops, then open the lid.
Drain, keeping some liquid. Blend the warm chickpeas with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt, adding cooking liquid until smooth.
Drizzle with olive oil.
Select Sauté and heat the pot. Heat the oil and lightly brown the eggplant for 4 minutes, then add the garlic.

Pour in the water and scrape the bottom of the inner pot clean, so nothing is stuck and the pot doesn't show a burn warning. An electric pressure cooker needs at least 1 cup (250 ml) of thin liquid to come up to pressure.
Lock the lid and turn the valve to Sealing. Pressure cook on High for 3 minutes. The pot first takes about 10 to 15 minutes to come up to pressure; that is not part of the cook time.
Quick release the pressure by turning the valve to Venting, keeping your hands and face away from the steam, then open the lid when the float valve drops.
Drain well and blend with tahini, lemon juice and salt.
Top with paprika and parsley.

Heat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and both sugars until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time and the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt and mix in on low speed until just combined; spoon and level the flour, or weigh it.
Stir in the white chocolate and macadamias.
Scoop rounded tablespoons 2 inches (5 cm) apart and bake for 9 to 11 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle.
Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.

Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until just set; cool before icing.

Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9x5-inch (23x13 cm) loaf pan.

Rub the zest into the sugar, then whisk in the eggs, milk, oil and 2 tbsp lemon juice. Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt. After baking, drizzle with the powdered sugar mixed with the remaining lemon juice.
Bake for about 50 minutes until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C).
Heat a 10-inch cast-iron skillet with 1 tbsp butter in the oven. Whisk the dry ingredients, then the eggs, buttermilk and remaining butter, and stir together. Pour into the hot skillet.
Bake for about 22 minutes until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9x5-inch (23x13 cm) loaf pan.
Pour the boiling water over the dates and baking soda and leave 15 minutes. Beat the butter, sugar and egg, stir in the dates and liquid, then the flour, salt and nuts.
Bake for about 55 minutes until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9x5-inch (23x13 cm) loaf pan.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir in the egg, milk and oil. Pour half in the pan, sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon, add the rest and swirl with a knife.
Bake for about 50 minutes until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9x5-inch (23x13 cm) loaf pan.
Beat the butter and sugar, then the eggs, milk and zest. Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, then the blueberries tossed in 1 tbsp flour.
Bake for about 60 minutes until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9x5-inch (23x13 cm) loaf pan.
Stir the flour, sugar and beer to a sticky batter, spread in the pan and pour the butter over the top.
Bake for about 50 minutes until a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and line two 9-inch (23 cm) round pans.
Beat the butter and sugar for 4 minutes until pale, then the eggs one at a time and the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt and add in three parts, alternating with the milk.
Divide between the pans and bake for 28 to 32 minutes.
Cool completely before frosting.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 10x15-inch (25x38 cm) sheet pan.
Whisk the flour, sugar, soda and salt. Bring half the butter, half the cocoa and the water to a boil and pour over; stir in the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes.
Meanwhile melt the rest of the butter and cocoa with the milk, beat in the powdered sugar and pecans, and pour over the warm cake.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and line two 9-inch pans.
Whisk the eggs, oil and sugars, then fold in the flour, soda, salt and cinnamon, then the carrots and walnuts.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes and cool.
Beat the cream cheese and butter, then the powdered sugar and vanilla, and frost.
Heat the oven to 325 °F (165 °C) and grease a 10-inch tube pan.
Beat the butter and sugar for 5 minutes, then the eggs one at a time.
Whisk the cake flour, baking powder and salt and add alternately with the sour cream and vanilla.
Bake for 65 to 75 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Beat the butter and sugar, then the egg and applesauce.
Fold in the dry ingredients and raisins.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C).
Whisk the dry ingredients in an 8-inch square pan, make three wells and pour the oil into one, the vinegar into another and the vanilla into the third.
Pour the water over and stir until smooth.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes. This cake contains no eggs, milk or butter.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 9-inch square pan.
Mix the brown sugar, cinnamon, pecans and 1/3 cup of the flour with 3 tbsp of the butter for the streusel.
Beat the rest of the butter with the sugar, then the eggs, sour cream and vanilla, and fold in the remaining flour, baking powder and salt.
Spread in the pan, scatter the streusel over and bake for 40 to 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and line an 8-inch square pan.
Melt the butter, stir in the sugar, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Stir in the cocoa, flour, salt and baking powder, then the chips.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until the top is set but a toothpick still shows moist crumbs.
Cool fully before cutting.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and line a 9-inch square pan.
Mix the flour, oats, sugar, soda, salt and butter to a crumble.
Press two-thirds into the pan, spread with jam and scatter the rest over.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes and cool before cutting.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C).
Mix the butter and crumbs and press into a 9x13-inch pan.
Layer the chips, coconut and pecans, then pour the condensed milk evenly over.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden; cool before cutting.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease a 10x15-inch pan.
Whisk the eggs, pumpkin, sugar and oil, then fold in the dry ingredients.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes and cool.
Beat the cream cheese, butter and powdered sugar and spread on top.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C). Do not grease the tube pan.
Sift the cake flour with half the sugar twice.
Whisk the whites, cream of tartar and salt to soft peaks, then add the rest of the sugar gradually to stiff glossy peaks and the vanilla.
Fold in the flour mixture in four parts, spoon into the pan and bake for 38 to 42 minutes.
Cool upside down in the pan.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, soda and salt.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs and butter, pour in and stir just until combined; leave lumpy and rest 5 minutes.
Cook 1/4 cup scoops on a lightly buttered griddle over medium heat until bubbles form, about 2 minutes, then flip for 1 minute.
Serve with maple syrup.
Heat the oven to 450 °F (230 °C).
Whisk the dry ingredients and grate or cut in the cold butter until in pea-sized pieces.
Stir in the buttermilk to a shaggy dough, pat out, fold in thirds twice and pat to 3/4 inch.
Cut straight down with a floured cutter without twisting and bake touching on a sheet for 12 to 14 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450 °F (230 °C).
Whisk the dry ingredients, then stir in the butter and milk just until combined.
Drop 1/4-cup mounds onto a lined sheet and bake for 12 to 14 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C).
Whisk the dry ingredients and zest, and cut in the butter.
Whisk the cream and egg, stir in, then fold in the blueberries.
Pat into a round, cut 8 wedges and bake for 18 to 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C) and grease an 8-inch square dish.
Mix the oats, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
Whisk the milk, eggs, butter and vanilla and stir in, then fold in the blueberries.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until set.
Heat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C) with a greased popover or muffin tin inside.
Whisk everything to a smooth batter.
Fill the hot cups halfway and bake for 20 minutes, then reduce to 350 °F (175 °C) for 15 minutes without opening the door.
Serve at once.
Blend everything except the spread until smooth and rest 15 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered 8-inch pan over medium heat, pour in 3 tbsp batter and swirl thin.
Cook 1 minute until the edges lift, flip and cook 30 seconds.
Fill with spread or fruit.
Heat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C) and line a muffin tin.
Beat the butter and sugar, then the eggs, sour cream and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, soda and salt.
Layer the batter with the brown sugar and cinnamon in the cases and bake for 18 to 20 minutes.
Whisk the flour, salt and sugar and cut in the butter until in pea-sized pieces.
Sprinkle in the ice water a tablespoon at a time, tossing, until the dough holds when squeezed.
Press into a disc, wrap and chill for at least 1 hour before rolling. Makes one 9-inch crust.
Heat the oven to 425 °F (220 °C).
Whisk the pumpkin, sugar, salt, spices and eggs, then the evaporated milk.
Pour into the crust and bake for 15 minutes, then reduce to 350 °F (175 °C) for 40 to 50 minutes until a knife comes out clean near the centre.
Cool for 2 hours.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C).
Whisk the syrup, eggs, sugar, butter and vanilla, stir in the pecans and pour into the crust.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until set with a slight wobble, covering the edges with foil if they darken.
Cool completely.
Heat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C).
Toss the apples with the sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a 9-inch square dish.
Rub the flour, oats, brown sugar and butter together and scatter over.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the fruit bubbles.
Heat the oven to 375 °F (190 °C) and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Mix the flour, 1 cup of the sugar, the baking powder and salt, cut in the butter and stir in the egg to a crumbly dough.
Press half into the pan.
Toss the berries with the remaining 1/2 cup sugar and the cornstarch, spread over and crumble the rest of the dough on top.
Bake for 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350 °F (175 °C).
Press the crumbs, sugar and butter into a 9-inch pie dish and bake for 10 minutes.
Whisk the condensed milk, yolks, lime juice and zest, pour in and bake for 15 minutes.
Chill for 3 hours and top with whipped cream.
Make the pastry by cutting the butter into the flour and salt and adding the water; chill 1 hour.
Simmer the cherries, sugar and cornstarch until thick and cool.
Roll the pastry, cut 16 rectangles, fill half with cherries, cover, crimp and brush with egg.
Bake at 400 °F (200 °C) for 20 to 22 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, flour and salt in a saucepan, then the milk and yolks, and cook over medium heat, stirring, until thick and bubbling.
Off the heat stir in the butter and vanilla.
Layer the bananas in the crust, pour over the custard and chill for 4 hours.
Top with whipped cream.

Shred, drain most of the liquid, stir in the barbecue sauce and serve in buns.
Put everything except the peas and cilantro in the slow cooker.

Season the beef and put it in the slow cooker with the vegetables, garlic, wine, tomatoes, paste and bay leaves.

Put everything except the noodles and parsley in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 7 hours or on High for 4 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Shred the chicken, add the noodles and cook on High for 20 minutes, then add parsley and season.
Put everything in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours or on High for 4 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Pull the meat off the hock, return it and season.
Put the pork, salsa, onion, garlic and cumin in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 8 hours or on High for 5 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Shred, add lime and cilantro, and serve in tortillas.
Put everything except the pasta and parmesan in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 7 hours or on High for 4 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Add the pasta and cook on High for 20 minutes, then season and top with parmesan.
Put the beef, stock, soy sauce, sugar, garlic and sesame oil in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 6 hours or on High for 3 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Stir in the cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water and the broccoli and cook on High for 30 minutes; serve over rice.
Put everything except the shrimp and rice in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 6 hours or on High for 3 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Add the shrimp for the last 20 minutes on High, then stir in the cooked rice.
Put the meatballs, stock, worcestershire and onion in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 5 hours or on High for 3 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream, stir in for the last 20 minutes, and serve over noodles with parsley.
Put everything except the cheese in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on Low for 3 hours or on High for 2 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Fluff and top with cheese.

Cover and cook on Low for 7 hours or on High for 4 hours, until tender. Slow cookers vary, so check toward the end.
Stir and serve with extra milk.
Put everything in the slow cooker.

Put everything in the slow cooker and whisk.

Score the eggs, add them and simmer 10 minutes more.
Season the beef and sear it in very hot oil in batches, 1 to 2 minutes, then set aside.
Stir-fry the onion and chili for 2 minutes, then the garlic and tomatoes for 1 minute.
Return the beef with the soy sauce and vinegar and toss.
Fold in the fries and cilantro and serve with rice.
Poach the chicken in salted water for 15 minutes, shred it and keep 250 ml of the broth.
Soak the bread in the milk and blend with the walnuts and parmesan.
Cook the onion, garlic and aji paste in the oil for 6 minutes, add the bread mixture and broth and simmer for 5 minutes until creamy.
Stir in the chicken and serve over rice with eggs and olives.
Boil the soaked beans hard for 10 minutes, then simmer with the carrot for 60 minutes until tender.
Fry the pork belly until crisp, then cook the onion, tomatoes, garlic, cumin and green onions in the fat for 8 minutes (this is the hogao).
Add the plantain and hogao to the beans and simmer 20 minutes more until thick.
Season and serve with rice, avocado and a fried egg.
Marinate the fish with lime juice, garlic and salt for 20 minutes.
Layer half the onion, peppers and tomatoes in a wide pot with the olive oil, add the fish and cover with the rest of the vegetables.
Pour over the coconut milk and dende oil and simmer covered for 15 to 20 minutes without stirring.
Scatter with cilantro and serve with rice.
Simmer the beans in plenty of water with the bay leaves for 45 minutes.
Brown the bacon, pork and sausage in a frying pan, then the onion and garlic.
Add everything to the beans and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes until the meat is tender and the broth thick.
Season and serve with rice and orange slices.
Finely chop the parsley and garlic and mix with the oregano, pepper flakes, vinegar, oil and salt; leave for 20 minutes.
Season the steak and grill or sear over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest for 10 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Spoon over the chimichurri.
Simmer the steak in salted water for 1 hour until tender, then shred it.
Cook the onion, pepper and garlic in 1 tbsp oil, add the cumin, tomatoes and shredded beef with a little broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Warm the beans with a pinch of cumin, and fry the plantain slices in the rest of the oil.
Serve the beef with rice, beans and plantain.
Cook the onion and pepper in the oil for 5 minutes, then the garlic.
Add the beef with the cumin and oregano and brown it.
Stir in the tomato sauce, olives, raisins and capers and simmer for 15 minutes.
Season and serve with rice.
Fry the ham in the oil, then the sofrito for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato paste, sazon and olives, then the rice and stir to coat.
Add the pigeon peas, water and salt, bring to a boil and cook uncovered until the water drops to the level of the rice.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Bring the beans and liquid, coconut milk and 250 ml water to a simmer with the green onions, thyme, whole pepper, allspice, garlic and salt.
Stir in the rice, return to a simmer, cover tightly and cook on low for 25 minutes.
Remove the aromatics (keep the pepper whole so it doesn't burst) and fluff.
Blend everything except the chicken into a paste (wear gloves for the peppers).
Rub over the chicken and marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Grill over medium heat or roast at 200 °C for 35 to 40 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through to 74 °C.
Serve with lime wedges.
Toast the chilies briefly, seed them and soak in hot water for 15 minutes.
Cook the onion and garlic in the oil, then blend with the chilies, tomatoes, almonds, half the sesame, raisins, spices and stock until very smooth.
Simmer the sauce for 15 minutes, stir in the chocolate and season.
Add the chicken and simmer covered for 25 minutes; top with the remaining sesame.
Char the poblanos under the grill until blistered, steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, peel and make a slit to remove the seeds.
Fill with cheese.
Simmer the tomato sauce with the onion, garlic and oregano for 10 minutes and pour into a baking dish.
Beat the whites stiff, fold in the yolks and flour, dip each pepper and set on the sauce.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
Heat the oven to 400 °F (200 °C).
Brown the beef and onion in the oil, add the spices, beans, tomatoes and corn and simmer for 10 minutes; pour into a baking dish.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, salt, egg, milk and half the cheese and spread over the filling.
Scatter with the remaining cheese and bake for 25 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Mix the salsa with the sour cream.
Mix the chicken with the onion, a third of the sauce and half the cheese.
Warm the tortillas, fill and roll them, and lay seam-side down in a dish.
Pour over the rest of the sauce and cheese and bake for 20 minutes; scatter with cilantro.
Blend the achiote, orange and lime juice, garlic, cumin, oregano and salt and marinate the pork overnight.
Wrap tightly in banana leaves or foil in a roasting dish and bake at 160 °C for 3 hours until it falls apart.
Meanwhile pickle the onion in the vinegar with a pinch of salt.
Shred the pork in its juices and serve in tortillas with the pickled onion.
Brown the chicken and chorizo in the oil in a paella pan or wide frying pan.
Add the onion and pepper for 5 minutes, then the garlic, paprika and saffron.
Stir in the tomatoes for 3 minutes, then scatter in the rice evenly and pour over the hot stock; season.
Simmer without stirring for 18 to 20 minutes, adding the peas for the last 5; turn the heat up for the last minute to form the socarrat.
Rest 5 minutes under a cloth and serve with lemon.
Warm the oil with the garlic and chili in a small frying pan over medium-low heat until the garlic is pale gold.
Turn up the heat, add the shrimp and paprika and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once.
Add the sherry and parsley and season.
Serve sizzling with bread.
Cook the onion and garlic in half the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, water and salt and simmer for 20 minutes until soft, then mash or blend.
Brown the chorizo separately.
Add the kale to the soup and simmer for 4 minutes, then top with the chorizo and the remaining oil.
Cook the pasta until just underdone and drain.
Brown the beef with the onion and garlic in the oil, add the cinnamon and tomatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick; off the heat whisk in the eggs, nutmeg and half the cheese.
Layer half the pasta, the meat, the rest of the pasta and the sauce in a dish and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 180 °C for 40 to 45 minutes and rest 15 minutes.
Simmer the soaked beans for 45 minutes to 1 hour until just tender and drain.
Cook the onion and carrots in the oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes, paste and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Mix with the beans and dill in a baking dish, add a splash of water, and bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes until thick.
Serve warm or at room temperature with feta.
Cook the onion and green onions in the oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice and tomato paste, then add the spinach in handfuls until wilted.
Pour in the stock, season, cover and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes.
Stir in the dill and lemon juice and serve with feta.
Heat the oven to 190 °C.
Cook the onion and garlic in 1 tbsp oil, stir into the passata and spread in a baking dish.
Arrange the vegetable slices upright in alternating rows over the sauce.
Drizzle with the rest of the oil, scatter with herbs, salt and pepper, cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover for 20 minutes.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the lentils, bay leaf and stock and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile fry the sausages for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Stir the mustard and vinegar into the lentils, season and serve with the sausages.
Beat the flour, eggs, milk, nutmeg and 1 tsp salt to a thick, sticky batter and rest for 10 minutes.
Fry the onions in 2 tbsp butter until deep golden, about 15 minutes.
Press the batter through a spaetzle maker or colander into simmering salted water; lift out when they float.
Layer the spaetzle with cheese in a buttered dish, keep warm until melted and top with the onions and chives.
Bring the vinegar, wine, 250 ml water, vegetables and spices to the boil, cool, and marinate the beef in it in the fridge for 2 to 3 days, turning daily.
Dry the beef, brown it in the oil in a heavy pot, add the strained marinade, cover and simmer gently for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Lift out the beef, stir the crushed gingersnaps and raisins into the liquid and simmer until thick.
Slice the beef and serve with the sauce.
Mix the flour, egg, water, oil and 1 tsp salt to a soft dough, knead 5 minutes and rest covered for 30 minutes.
Fry the onions in the butter until golden; mix half into the potato and cheese and season well.
Roll the dough thin, cut 7 cm rounds, fill with a spoonful, fold and pinch firmly closed.
Boil in batches until they float plus 2 minutes, then toss with the rest of the onions and butter and serve with sour cream.
Brown the chicken in the oil and set aside.
Cook the onions for 8 minutes, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika so it doesn't burn.
Add the pepper, tomato, stock and chicken, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream, stir it in and simmer 3 minutes; season and serve with noodles.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then the garlic.
Add the beans with their liquid and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing about half.
Stir in the walnuts, spices and vinegar and simmer 5 minutes.
Season and fold in plenty of cilantro.
Fry the potatoes in 2 tbsp butter over medium-high heat until golden and crisp, about 12 minutes.
Add the onion and meat and fry 8 minutes more; season.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the butter.
Serve the hash topped with an egg, with pickled beets and parsley.
Brown the beef with the vegetables in the oil, stir in the paste and flour, then the stock and worcestershire, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until soft and mash with the butter and milk.
Spoon the filling into a dish, top with the mash and cheese.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 to 30 minutes until golden.
Boil the potatoes until soft.
Meanwhile cook the cabbage in 1 tbsp butter with a splash of water until tender, about 6 minutes.
Warm the milk with the green onions.
Mash the potatoes with the milk and the rest of the butter, fold in the cabbage and season.
Poach the haddock in the milk and water for 5 minutes, lift out and flake it, keeping the liquid.
Cook the onion and leek in the butter for 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes and poaching liquid and simmer for 15 minutes until soft; mash a few potatoes.
Add the fish, heat through, season with pepper and add chives.
Season and flour the chicken.
Fry in the oil and 1 tbsp butter for 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the garlic, wine, stock, lemon juice and capers and simmer for 3 minutes.
Swirl in the rest of the butter, return the chicken and scatter with parsley.
Lay a sage leaf and a slice of prosciutto on each escalope and secure with a toothpick.
Dust the underside with flour.
Fry prosciutto-side down in the oil and butter for 2 minutes, then turn for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the wine, let it bubble for a minute and spoon the sauce over.
Cook the onion and pancetta in 2 tbsp butter for 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time with the peas, stirring, for 18 minutes; it should stay soupy.
Stir in the rest of the butter, parmesan and parsley, and season.
Brown the onion and lamb with the turmeric in 1 tbsp oil, add the water and simmer for 1 hour.
Fry the herbs in the remaining oil for 15 minutes until dark and fragrant, then add the fenugreek.
Add the herbs, dried limes and salt to the lamb and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes.
Add the beans for the last 15 minutes and serve with rice.
Soak the rice for 30 minutes, then boil in salted water for 6 minutes and drain.
Blanch the orange zest twice, then warm it with the dried fruit, sugar and 1 tbsp butter for 3 minutes.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in the pot, layer the rice with the fruit and cardamom, make a few holes with a spoon handle and drizzle with the saffron steeped in 3 tbsp hot water and the last butter.
Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid and steam on low for 35 minutes; top with the nuts.
Marinate the chicken with the spices, garlic, lemon juice, oil and salt for at least 1 hour.
Roast at 220 °C for 20 to 25 minutes or grill until charred.
Rest and slice thinly.
Wrap in flatbreads with the garlic sauce, tomato and pickles.
Peel the eggplants in stripes, slit each lengthways without cutting through, salt them for 20 minutes and pat dry.
Fry them in half the oil until browned all over.
Cook the onions slowly in the rest of the oil for 10 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes, sugar, salt and parsley.
Stuff the eggplants, set in a dish with 120 ml water and lemon juice and bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes; serve at room temperature.
Cook the peppers in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chili flakes and simmer for 6 minutes until thick.
Add the beaten eggs and stir gently until just softly set.
Season and scatter with parsley; serve with bread.
Salt the eggplant slices and fry in the oil until golden on both sides; drain.
Mix the tomato, cucumber and parsley as a salad.
Spread the pitas with hummus and fill with eggplant, sliced egg, salad, tahini sauce and amba.
Knead the flour, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest 20 minutes.
Mix the potato with the chili, spices, cilantro and salt.
Roll a ball of dough to a small circle, put a ball of filling in the centre, gather the edges, seal and roll gently to 18 cm.
Cook on a hot griddle, brushing with ghee, for 2 minutes per side until spotted golden.
Serve with yogurt.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, then the onion for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and spices, then the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the beans and water and simmer for 20 minutes, mashing a few beans.
Season and add cilantro.
Char the eggplants over a gas flame or under the grill, turning, until collapsed and smoky, about 15 minutes; peel and mash.
Fry the cumin seeds in the oil, then the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic, ginger and chili.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, then the eggplant and garam masala for 5 minutes more.
Season and add cilantro.
Fry the chicken in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, chilies, spices and salt.
Cook uncovered, stirring, for 15 minutes until the tomatoes break down and the oil separates.
Stir in the yogurt and garam masala for 3 minutes and finish with cilantro and julienned ginger.
Knead the flour and water to a firm dough and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, cilantro, cumin, soy and salt.
Roll small thin rounds, fill and pleat closed.
Steam on oiled parchment for 12 minutes.
Blend the roasted tomatoes and chili with salt for the dipping sauce.
Cook the beef with the soy sauce and half the sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach and sprouts and season each with sesame oil and salt; quickly saute the carrot, zucchini and mushrooms separately.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Divide the rice into bowls, arrange the vegetables and beef on top, add an egg and serve with gochujang and sesame; mix everything before eating.
Fry the pork in the oil until it renders, then add the kimchi and fry for 4 minutes.
Stir in the gochugaru and gochujang, add the water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Slide in the tofu and simmer 5 minutes.
Add green onions and sesame oil and serve with rice.
Simmer the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar in a small frying pan, add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer for 6 minutes until cooked.
Pour over the eggs in a circle, cover and cook for 1 minute until just set.
Slide over bowls of rice and top with green onions.
Brown the beef in the oil, then add the onion, potatoes and carrots and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar, bring to a simmer and skim.
Cover with a smaller lid resting on the food and simmer for 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the green beans for the last 3 minutes.
Mix the pork with half the fish sauce, the sugar, shallots and garlic and shape into small patties; rest 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred.
Warm the nuoc cham with a splash of water and the carrot.
Serve the patties in bowls of the sauce with noodles, lettuce and herbs alongside for dipping.
Melt the sugar in a heavy pot until deep amber, then carefully add the pork and stir to coat.
Add the fish sauce, shallots, garlic and coconut water, bring to a simmer and cook covered for 30 minutes.
Add the eggs and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce is sticky.
Season with pepper and scatter with green onions.
Cook the chicken in a dry pan with 3 tbsp water, breaking it up, for 6 to 8 minutes until just cooked.
Off the heat, stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and chili.
Add the rice powder, shallots and herbs and toss.
Serve warm or at room temperature with lettuce cups.
Fry the shallots, garlic, chili and shrimp paste in 2 tbsp oil for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Add the rice, kecap manis and soy and stir-fry over high heat for 4 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the rest of the oil and serve on top with cucumber and fried shallots.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and fish sauce and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the water and simmer for 20 minutes, skimming.
Add the papaya and simmer 8 minutes until tender, then the spinach for 1 minute; season with pepper.
Soak the noodles in warm water for 10 minutes and drain.
Cook the onion and garlic in the oil, then the chicken for 4 minutes.
Add the carrot, cabbage and snow peas for 2 minutes, then the soy and stock and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and toss until they absorb the liquid; serve with lemon wedges.
Toss the tuna with the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, green onions and sesame seeds; chill for 15 minutes.
Divide the rice between bowls.
Top with the tuna, avocado, cucumber and nori. Use only fish sold for eating raw.
Fry the pork in the oil until crisp, then the bean paste, black beans, garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the stock and slide in the tofu; simmer for 5 minutes without stirring too much.
Thicken with the cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water.
Sprinkle with the ground peppercorns and green onions and serve with rice.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and scramble softly in 1 tbsp hot oil; tip out while still wet.
Add the rest of the oil and the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes until juicy, with the sugar, ketchup and salt.
Return the eggs and fold through.
Scatter with green onions and serve over rice.
Cook the grain in salted water according to the packet and drain or fluff.

Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Toss the vegetables that need cooking with the oil, any spice and salt and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once (keep cucumber, cabbage, leaves and fresh tomatoes raw).
Cook or warm the protein: pan-fry tofu, tempeh, chicken or shrimp until golden and cooked through; just rinse and drain canned beans.
Whisk the dressing ingredients with a splash of water and salt to taste.
Build the bowls: grain first, then the vegetables and protein, a spoonful of dressing and the toppings.
Cook the grain in salted water according to the packet and drain or fluff.
